PLETT CULT

By: Latashia Naidoo | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A small town murder, linked to a spiritual cult.

Unique Selling Point:
One man wreaked havoc across the Garden Route for over two decades. But it would take the murder of a former police detective for him to face the law.

Summary:
Plettenberg Bay is widely seen as a low-crime, holiday town - not a place associated with violent
death.
But on Sunday, 18 January 2026, that perception was shattered when Nicky van Heerden, a
54-year-old former police detective, was found dead near the Keurbooms River after reports of
a woman screaming.
The man charged with her murder is Bevan van Druten, a Garden Route driftwood sculptor
whose work has appeared widely both locally and internationally.
He denies the charge; the State is opposing bail.
What makes this a Carte Blanche story is what existed before that night. Long before Nicky met
him, at least six women had already sought protection orders against Van Druten, alleging
intimidation and threatening behaviour. Each case was treated in isolation, no escalation
followed.

Since Van Druten’s arrest, residents - including pensioners - have told media they were terrified
of him for years, claims police say are not part of the murder case but which raise serious
questions about what was known and ignored.

Then there’s the voice note. Ten minutes and 29 seconds long, recorded shortly before Nicky’s
death and sent to WhatsApp contacts. According to reporting, it reflects fear and distress and is
now with investigators as they reconstruct her final hours.

Nicky was not naïve, she was a detective. So how does someone trained to assess danger end
up dead when warning signs were already on record?
This story is about how systems fail when risk is documented but never connected.

Press Release:


Murder in Paradise
January 2026: Plettenberg Bay’s post-holiday peace is shattered when a woman’s body is found near the Keurbooms River. But in the aftermath of her death, dark details emerge. A rambling voice note vividly illustrates the dead woman’s fear and distress. Residents claim she belonged to a shadowy cult. Across the Garden Route, other women come forward with allegations of intimidation and abuse. Why were so many cases treated in isolation? What led a former police detective to her death? And will one murder end an alleged decades-long reign of fear?
Producer: Latashia Naidoo | Presenter: Lourensa Eckard

Script:


PLETT CULT - FINAL:

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“Listen to me, listen to me, all of you. I am not a f****** follower.”

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“I know, I know, I seen this s*** before. I felt the pain of Jesus Christ! The fear, I felt the fear. You have to listen to me! Please! Please!”

LOURENSA: Just hours after recording this voice note, the person behind it… was dead.

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“The Lord is busy talking to me.

LOURENSA: In a crime that’s rocked a small coastal town…

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“Bevan van Druten is sitting next to me. He was attacked by a demon, the legion of demons.”

LOURENSA: Two local men become the focus.

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“We are an army of angels. We are going to f### you up Rocco Viljoen, and your f###ing legion of demons.”

AMAURE DE VILLIERS: “It’s like he goes into this total possessed manic thing, where I personally don’t think he even knows what he’s doing.”

VO: Nicky van Heerden was 54. A former police detective who grew up in Plettenberg Bay, she had recently moved back home.

VO: In the years before her death, a divorce ended both her marriage and her career in policing, and she began searching for a more spiritual path.
NICKY VAN HEERDEN: ‘And then through divine alignment these people came on my path…”
LOURENSA: She started calling herself ‘Alaska Runwithwolves’, and joined a small circle of artists and spiritualists along the Garden Route.
SAMANTHA CARTWRIGHT: “She was very lighthearted, beautiful woman, strong - we used to call her the ‘Amazonian Goddess’ you know, because she is, she’s Amazonian… we spent a lot of time together in moments of connection”

VO: She found connection with a group that promised spirituality and healing - led by a man by the name of Rocco Viljoen.

LOURENSA: ‘How would you describe her?’
ROCCO VILJOEN: “I would describe her as a woman who lost everything in her life, who hid pain behind a smile. She had a good heart, and always wanted to help people and be loving.”

LINK: “In the days before Nicky’s lifeless body was found - right over there - she started dating a man called Bevan van Druten, and this is where he lived.”

LOURENSA: Nicky met van Druten, a local driftwood artist, in December last year at a Summer Solstice event on the Garden Route.

VO: A whirlwind romance followed.

LINK: “Friends say the relationship moved at speed. Within days, Nicky was introducing Bevan as her ‘husband’. Those same friends say that her behaviour had also started to change - her language, her beliefs, her sense of reality.”
LOURENSA: Then, on January 18th, police were called to a gated estate near the Keurbooms River, after reports of a woman screaming.
LOURENSA: When they arrived, they found Nicky’s body beside a car in the nearby dunes. She’d been badly beaten.
LOURENSA: In the days that followed, investigators pieced together what had happened.
LOURENSA: And then they discovered the voicenote.
VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“I am telling you now, please listen to me, listen to me, listen to me. The Lord is busy talking to me. Bevan van Druten is sitting next to me. He was attacked by a demon, the legion of demons. Rocco i don’t know if you’re an instrument or not.”

LOURENSA: Sent to a private spiritual WhatsApp group, it’s the last time those close to her heard Nicky’s voice.
LOURENSA: In it, she names both Van Druten and Viljoen. She describes the former as a saviour, the latter as a demon.
LOURENSA: Both now stand at the centre of the case: van Druten accused of murder, and Viljoen of leading a cult.
VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“I must save people. You, my entire family, are sitting on the wrong side of this f***ing army.”

LOURENSA: “Is there a name for the community you live in?’
ROCCO VILJOEN: “Nothing. Nothing. We call it a circle of friends. You misunderstand because people have said ‘Rocco’s cult.’ And there is nothing. It’s Rocco sitting on his chair telling his stories and now and then someone comes to visit and says, “Hey Rocco. Shall we have coffee?” And that’s it. There is absolutely nothing more than that.”
LOURENSA:‘So, it’s not a cult?’
ROCCO VILJOEN: “Nothing. It’s a made-up story that exist.”

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“I love you terribly. Please. You are following the wrong guy. Get off his group immediately.”

LOURENSA: In a more than 10 minute tirade, Nicky calls Viljoen a ‘false prophet’ and urges people to leave the group.

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“Rocco, f### you, I have felt you for a long time with your sexual, predatory. Now, take your cats and your trailer park and park it far.”

LOURENSA: ‘In that voicenote, she also refers to you as a “sexual predator”.’
ROCCO VILJOEN: “That’s correct, yes.”
LOURENSA: ‘In reference to you. What is your response?’
ROCCO VILJOEN: “Luckily, we never had anything sexual. And you’re welcome to ask anyone if I had a sexual relationship with anyone.”
LOURENSA: ‘So, the voice note she uses biblical terms and she talks about demons, and that she needs to gather angels to fight a demon army led by you.”

ROCCO VILJOEN: “I think he forced her to say that, I think he brainwashed her and told her what to say. And I think that’s why he killed her, because she probably told him, I’m going to tell Rocco that you forced me.”

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
NICKY VAN HEERDEN: “This [inaudible] next to me is laughing. It’s Bevan van Druten.”
BEVAN VAN DRUTEN: ‘The boxer.’
NICKY VAN HEERDEN: “The boxer who has two guns. “

LOURENSA: ‘You can hear Bevan is present when she records the voice note…’
ROCCO VILJOEN: “Yes, you can hear him laughing in the background.”
LOURENSA: ‘What do you make of that?”

ROCCO VILJOEN: “I think if the detectives dig a bit deeper, and go through her recording history, the’ll see it was done [recorded] a few times, and deleted, done and deleted… I’m not saying it for a fact, but I believe it.”

LOURENSA: ‘You see the video [voice note] as a cry for help, not an accusation?’’
ROCCO VILJOEN: “Yes… I think she tried to warn me, and I think that man had a grudge against me and has one still.”

LINK: “The Garden Route sells itself as an escape: quiet roads, weekend markets, holiday homes, and breathtaking views. People come here to feel safe. That’s why Nicky’s murder has shaken the community to its core - from Plettenberg Bay to George. Because the danger didn’t come from outside; it was already here.”

LOURENSA: Bevan van Druten was a popular figure in this part of the southern Cape. One with a chequered past.

LOURENSA: In May last year, Van Druten and Viljoen eventually crossed swords, after Van Druten allegedly abused his girlfriend at the time, one of Viljoen’s friends - Helene Botha.

LOURENSA: They were together for less than a month but she ended the relationship after van Druten allegedly became controlling and threatening.

HELENE BOTHA: “It’s the same story with a lot of the victims: he meets you, he romanticises you, he isolates you, and then when it’s almost too late, when you try to say no - when you try to say no to anything that isn’t what he wants - then suddenly the ‘snap’, the snap is just there.”
LOURENSA: Van Druten allegedly refused to let the relationship end. Helene says he threatened her one night - appeared at her farm unannounced, in a frenzied state.
HELENE BOTHA: “I realised that he’s probably gonna want to come see me. So I went to my neighbour’s house crying, saying that I’m really scared, and I’d just feel better to physically be with somebody.”
LOURENSA: "That neighbour was Viljoen, and the two men reportedly came to blows. The next day Helene applied for a restraining order.”

HELENE BOTHA : “I decided to travel with an axe in my car for physical protection. It’s eight months later and it’s still in my car…”

LOURENSA: “You’re shaking, like you have a physical reaction when you talk about this. Are you still traumatised?”
HELENE BOTHA: “I’m still traumatised. I’m still in shock that this level of cruelty could walk among us, that I was fooled for one.”

LOURENSA: As more and more alleged victims of Bevan van Druten emerge, a pattern of fear and control becomes apparent.

LOURENSA: “So he physically assaulted you?”
AMAURE: “Yes he did. He punched me… and he literally dragged me by my hair out onto the pavement, and started kicking me while I was down on the ground.”

LOURENSA: In 2022, Amaure De Villiers was Viljoen's neighbour in Sedgefield, around 50km from Plett.

AMAURE: “I permanently wore a panic button around my neck. When I was in my car, when I was watering the garden, gardening, whatever, I permanently had my panic button on.”

LOURENSA: ‘And this was a man with violent tendencies.’
AMAURE DE VILLIERS: “Yes.”
LOURENSA: ‘It’s outrageous to think what he did to you and that he basically got off.’
AMAURE DE VILLIERS: “Well it’s outrageous to think how long this has been going on for. I mean, I wasn’t the first. There were lots of women before me. So this has been going on for years, all over the Garden Route.’

SAMANTHA CARTWRIGHT: “At first you just think he’s an artist, you know, one of those geeky artists, but once you feel his energy - for me it felt very narcissistic, sociopathic, we definitely figured out that he’s a pathological liar…”

LOURENSA: Samantha Cartwright is a victims’ advocate - and was a close friend of Nicky’s. She claims she spent years warning women in her spiritual community about Van Druten.

SAMANTHA CARTWRIGHT: “This guy has been drifting all over the world. I think, we’re all here healing hey, we left big city to come here and heal, and this oke has been terrorising it.”

LOURENSA: And if Bevan van Druten is guilty, these warnings were too late.

LOURENSA: The criminal case against Bevan van Druten has yet to be tested in court. He will undergo psychiatric evaluation at Valkenberg Hospital in Cape Town. The defence has withdrawn its bail application.

LOURENSA: But the fear described by multiple women across the Garden Route is already on record. Taken together, they describe a pattern of alleged behaviour that escalated over time.

LOURENSA: ‘Was there a part of you that felt like that could have been you?’
HELENE BOTHA: “There’s a very big part of me that felt it could’ve been me, and that really woke me up to the fact that life is so precious.”

NICKY VAN HEERDEN: ‘Start feeling it, that vibration…’

LOURENSA: For those who loved Nicky van Heerden, she is remembered for her light. And for what was lost.

VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN:
“God, I am so sorry.
I am so sorry.
I am so sorry.”

NICKY VAN HEERDEN: ‘Check you on the flip side.’

FTB.

Rocco i don’t know if you’re an instrument or not.” LOURENSA: Sent to a private spiritual WhatsApp group, it’s the last time those close to her heard Nicky’s voice. LOURENSA: In it, she names both Van Druten and Viljoen. She describes the former as a saviour, the latter as a demon. LOURENSA: Both now stand at the centre of the case: van Druten accused of murder, and Viljoen of leading a cult. VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN: “I must save people. You, my entire family, are sitting on the wrong side of this f***ing army.” LOURENSA: “Is there a name for the community you live in?’ ROCCO VILJOEN: “Nothing. Nothing. We call it a circle of friends. You misunderstand because people have said ‘Rocco’s cult.’ And there is nothing. It’s Rocco sitting on his chair telling his stories and now and then someone comes to visit and says, “Hey Rocco. Shall we have coffee?” And that’s it. There is absolutely nothing more than that.” LOURENSA:‘So, it’s not a cult?’ ROCCO VILJOEN: “Nothing. It’s a made-up story that exist.” VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN: “I love you terribly. Please. You are following the wrong guy. Get off his group immediately.” LOURENSA: In a more than 10 minute tirade, Nicky calls Viljoen a ‘false prophet’ and urges people to leave the group. VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN: “Rocco, f### you, I have felt you for a long time with your sexual, predatory. Now, take your cats and your trailer park and park it far.” LOURENSA: ‘In that voicenote, she also refers to you as a “sexual predator”.’ ROCCO VILJOEN: “That’s correct, yes.” LOURENSA: ‘In reference to you. What is your response?’ ROCCO VILJOEN: “Luckily, we never had anything sexual. And you’re welcome to ask anyone if I had a sexual relationship with anyone.” LOURENSA: ‘So, the voice note she uses biblical terms and she talks about demons, and that she needs to gather angels to fight a demon army led by you.” ROCCO VILJOEN: “I think he forced her to say that, I think he brainwashed her and told her what to say. And I think that’s why he killed her, because she probably told him, I’m going to tell Rocco that you forced me.” VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN: NICKY VAN HEERDEN: “This [inaudible] next to me is laughing. It’s Bevan van Druten.” BEVAN VAN DRUTEN: ‘The boxer.’ NICKY VAN HEERDEN: “The boxer who has two guns. “ LOURENSA: ‘You can hear Bevan is present when she records the voice note…’ ROCCO VILJOEN: “Yes, you can hear him laughing in the background.” LOURENSA: ‘What do you make of that?” ROCCO VILJOEN: “I think if the detectives dig a bit deeper, and go through her recording history, the’ll see it was done [recorded] a few times, and deleted, done and deleted… I’m not saying it for a fact, but I believe it.” LOURENSA: ‘You see the video [voice note] as a cry for help, not an accusation?’’ ROCCO VILJOEN: “Yes… I think she tried to warn me, and I think that man had a grudge against me and has one still.” LINK: “The Garden Route sells itself as an escape: quiet roads, weekend markets, holiday homes, and breathtaking views. People come here to feel safe. That’s why Nicky’s murder has shaken the community to its core - from Plettenberg Bay to George. Because the danger didn’t come from outside; it was already here.” LOURENSA: Bevan van Druten was a popular figure in this part of the southern Cape. One with a chequered past. LOURENSA: In May last year, Van Druten and Viljoen eventually crossed swords, after Van Druten allegedly abused his girlfriend at the time, one of Viljoen’s friends - Helene Botha. LOURENSA: They were together for less than a month but she ended the relationship after van Druten allegedly became controlling and threatening. HELENE BOTHA: “It’s the same story with a lot of the victims: he meets you, he romanticises you, he isolates you, and then when it’s almost too late, when you try to say no - when you try to say no to anything that isn’t what he wants - then suddenly the ‘snap’, the snap is just there.” LOURENSA: Van Druten allegedly refused to let the relationship end. Helene says he threatened her one night - appeared at her farm unannounced, in a frenzied state. HELENE BOTHA: “I realised that he’s probably gonna want to come see me. So I went to my neighbour’s house crying, saying that I’m really scared, and I’d just feel better to physically be with somebody.” LOURENSA: "That neighbour was Viljoen, and the two men reportedly came to blows. The next day Helene applied for a restraining order.” HELENE BOTHA : “I decided to travel with an axe in my car for physical protection. It’s eight months later and it’s still in my car…” LOURENSA: “You’re shaking, like you have a physical reaction when you talk about this. Are you still traumatised?” HELENE BOTHA: “I’m still traumatised. I’m still in shock that this level of cruelty could walk among us, that I was fooled for one.” LOURENSA: As more and more alleged victims of Bevan van Druten emerge, a pattern of fear and control becomes apparent. LOURENSA: “So he physically assaulted you?” AMAURE: “Yes he did. He punched me… and he literally dragged me by my hair out onto the pavement, and started kicking me while I was down on the ground.” LOURENSA: In 2022, Amaure De Villiers was Viljoen's neighbour in Sedgefield, around 50km from Plett. AMAURE: “I permanently wore a panic button around my neck. When I was in my car, when I was watering the garden, gardening, whatever, I permanently had my panic button on.” LOURENSA: ‘And this was a man with violent tendencies.’ AMAURE DE VILLIERS: “Yes.” LOURENSA: ‘It’s outrageous to think what he did to you and that he basically got off.’ AMAURE DE VILLIERS: “Well it’s outrageous to think how long this has been going on for. I mean, I wasn’t the first. There were lots of women before me. So this has been going on for years, all over the Garden Route.’ SAMANTHA CARTWRIGHT: “At first you just think he’s an artist, you know, one of those geeky artists, but once you feel his energy - for me it felt very narcissistic, sociopathic, we definitely figured out that he’s a pathological liar…” LOURENSA: Samantha Cartwright is a victims’ advocate - and was a close friend of Nicky’s. She claims she spent years warning women in her spiritual community about Van Druten. SAMANTHA CARTWRIGHT: “This guy has been drifting all over the world. I think, we’re all here healing hey, we left big city to come here and heal, and this oke has been terrorising it.” LOURENSA: And if Bevan van Druten is guilty, these warnings were too late. LOURENSA: The criminal case against Bevan van Druten has yet to be tested in court. He will undergo psychiatric evaluation at Valkenberg Hospital in Cape Town. The defence has withdrawn its bail application. LOURENSA: But the fear described by multiple women across the Garden Route is already on record. Taken together, they describe a pattern of alleged behaviour that escalated over time. LOURENSA: ‘Was there a part of you that felt like that could have been you?’ HELENE BOTHA: “There’s a very big part of me that felt it could’ve been me, and that really woke me up to the fact that life is so precious.” NICKY VAN HEERDEN: ‘Start feeling it, that vibration…’ LOURENSA: For those who loved Nicky van Heerden, she is remembered for her light. And for what was lost. VOICENOTE - NICKY VAN HEERDEN: “God, I am so sorry. I am so sorry. I am so sorry.” NICKY VAN HEERDEN: ‘Check you on the flip side.’ FTB.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A small town murder, linked to a spiritual cult.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: One man wreaked havoc across the Garden Route for over two decades. But it would take the murder of a former police detective for him to face the law.
metadata.Summary: Plettenberg Bay is widely seen as a low-crime, holiday town - not a place associated with violent death. But on Sunday, 18 January 2026, that perception was shattered when Nicky van Heerden, a 54-year-old former police detective, was found dead near the Keurbooms River after reports of a woman screaming. The man charged with her murder is Bevan van Druten, a Garden Route driftwood sculptor whose work has appeared widely both locally and internationally. He denies the charge; the State is opposing bail. What makes this a Carte Blanche story is what existed before that night. Long before Nicky met him, at least six women had already sought protection orders against Van Druten, alleging intimidation and threatening behaviour. Each case was treated in isolation, no escalation followed. Since Van Druten’s arrest, residents - including pensioners - have told media they were terrified of him for years, claims police say are not part of the murder case but which raise serious questions about what was known and ignored. Then there’s the voice note. Ten minutes and 29 seconds long, recorded shortly before Nicky’s death and sent to WhatsApp contacts. According to reporting, it reflects fear and distress and is now with investigators as they reconstruct her final hours. Nicky was not naïve, she was a detective. So how does someone trained to assess danger end up dead when warning signs were already on record? This story is about how systems fail when risk is documented but never connected.
